notice: Offline corpus for the Research Library. Summaries are original one-line descriptions written for this project, not publisher abstracts. Citation edges are a curated approximation of intellectual lineage used so the citation graph is populated without network access; when a live provider returns reference data it supersedes these edges. citation_count is 0 here on purpose - the API reports in-corpus in-degree instead of inventing counts.

papers.title: Stochastic Games
papers.summary: Introduces stochastic games: play moves between states according to a transition law driven by the players' joint actions, and establishes the existence of a value for the discounted case. The direct ancestor of every Markov-game formulation used here.

papers.title: Q-learning
papers.summary: Proves convergence of the incremental off-policy temporal-difference control rule that underpins the stage-2 MDP policy in this project.

papers.title: Markov games as a framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning
papers.summary: Recasts multi-agent RL as a zero-sum Markov game and introduces minimax-Q. The paper that made 'Markov game' the standard vocabulary for multi-agent decision problems.

papers.title: Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
papers.summary: The canonical treatment of POMDPs: belief-state planning under partial observability, which is the formal justification for maintaining an explicit belief distribution instead of a scalar confidence.

papers.title: Policy invariance under reward transformations: Theory and application to reward shaping
papers.summary: Shows that potential-based shaping is the only form of reward transformation that leaves the optimal policy unchanged. The reason the shaping terms in this project's reward are potential-like differences rather than raw bonuses.

papers.title: Between MDPs and semi-MDPs: A framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning
papers.summary: The options framework for temporally extended actions. Invoking an agent is naturally an option, which is the roadmap's path to hierarchical orchestration.

papers.title: Multiagent Systems: A Survey from a Machine Learning Perspective
papers.summary: Surveys multiagent systems through a learning lens and lays out the homogeneous/heterogeneous and communicating/non-communicating axes still used to classify agent architectures.

papers.title: Friend-or-Foe Q-learning in General-Sum Games
papers.summary: Splits general-sum games into coordination and adversarial cases with provable convergence in each. The 'friend' branch is the cooperative setting this project's stage-3 policy assumes.

papers.title: Finite-time Analysis of the Multiarmed Bandit Problem
papers.summary: Establishes UCB1 and logarithmic regret bounds. The optimism-under-uncertainty principle behind the exploration bonus in the stage-1 LinUCB policy.

papers.title: Multiagent learning using a variable learning rate
papers.summary: The WoLF principle: learn quickly when losing, slowly when winning. A practical answer to non-stationarity when several agents adapt at once.

papers.title: Nash Q-Learning for General-Sum Stochastic Games
papers.summary: Extends Q-learning to general-sum stochastic games by using stage-game Nash equilibria as the bootstrap target, with the conditions required for convergence.

papers.title: Potential-based shaping and Q-value initialization are equivalent
papers.summary: Proves potential-based shaping is equivalent to initializing Q-values with the potential function, which makes shaping a statement about priors rather than about the objective.

papers.title: Bandit based Monte-Carlo Planning
papers.summary: Introduces UCT, applying UCB1 to tree search. The bridge between bandit exploration and sequential planning that this project's roadmap follows.

papers.title: A Contextual-Bandit Approach to Personalized News Article Recommendation
papers.summary: Introduces LinUCB and offline replay evaluation for contextual bandits. This is the algorithm implemented verbatim as the stage-1 orchestration policy.

papers.title: Theoretical considerations of potential-based reward shaping for multi-agent systems
papers.summary: Extends the policy-invariance guarantee of potential-based shaping to multi-agent settings, showing Nash equilibria are preserved. Directly relevant to shaping a cooperative orchestration game.

papers.title: Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoff Functions
papers.summary: Provides the regret analysis for the linear contextual bandit family that LinUCB belongs to.

papers.title: Bayesian Active Learning for Classification and Preference Learning
papers.summary: Formulates acquisition as maximizing mutual information between observations and model parameters (BALD). The formal basis for treating expected information gain as an orchestration objective.

papers.title: A Survey of Monte Carlo Tree Search Methods
papers.summary: Comprehensive survey of MCTS variants and enhancements; the reference text for the tree-search planner on this project's roadmap.

papers.title: Thompson Sampling for Contextual Bandits with Linear Payoffs
papers.summary: Gives the first regret bounds for Thompson sampling in the linear contextual setting, the posterior-sampling alternative to the UCB bonus used in stage 1.

papers.title: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search
papers.summary: Combines learned value and policy networks with MCTS. The clearest demonstration that a learned value function plus search beats either alone - the argument for stage 2 plus planning.

papers.title: A Concise Introduction to Decentralized POMDPs
papers.summary: The reference treatment of Dec-POMDPs: cooperative multi-agent decision making under partial observability, and the exact formalism for orchestrating agents that each see only part of the task state.

papers.title: Outrageously Large Neural Networks: The Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts Layer
papers.summary: Sparse gating that routes each input to a small subset of experts. The parametric ancestor of agent routing: a learned gate deciding who does the work.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Actor-Critic for Mixed Cooperative-Competitive Environments
papers.summary: MADDPG: centralized critics with decentralized actors, the template for centralized-training / decentralized-execution used by most modern MARL systems.

papers.title: Value-Decomposition Networks For Cooperative Multi-Agent Learning
papers.summary: Decomposes a team value function into an additive sum of per-agent utilities so a shared reward can train independent learners. Implemented directly as the mixing rule in the stage-4 policy.

papers.title: Counterfactual Multi-Agent Policy Gradients
papers.summary: COMA: a counterfactual baseline that marginalizes one agent's action to measure its individual contribution. The credit-assignment idea behind this project's difference-reward head.

papers.title: QMIX: Monotonic Value Function Factorisation for Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Replaces VDN's additive mixing with a monotonic mixing network, expanding representable value functions while keeping decentralized argmax consistent with the joint argmax.

papers.title: QTRAN: Learning to Factorize with Transformation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Removes the additivity and monotonicity constraints of VDN and QMIX by learning a transformed joint action-value function.

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.summary: Couples a parametric generator with a non-parametric retriever. The reference model for what this project's Memory and Research agents actually do.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning: A Selective Overview of Theories and Algorithms
papers.summary: Maps MARL theory onto the Markov-game formalism and separates the cooperative, competitive and mixed settings with their respective convergence results.

papers.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Shows that eliciting intermediate reasoning steps improves multi-step problem solving, establishing the decomposition primitive the Planner agent models.

papers.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of PPO in Cooperative Multi-Agent Games
papers.summary: Demonstrates that on-policy PPO with shared parameters is competitive with specialized off-policy MARL methods, given the right implementation details.

papers.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.summary: Interleaves reasoning traces with tool actions in a single loop. The minimal single-agent baseline that this project's multi-agent policies are compared against.

papers.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
papers.summary: Self-supervised learning of when and how to call APIs, filtered by whether the call reduces prediction loss - an information-gain criterion for tool invocation.

papers.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Converts episodic failure into natural-language feedback stored in memory. The Critic plus Memory loop in this project is the structured analogue.

papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.summary: A memory-stream architecture with retrieval, reflection and planning that produces believable multi-agent behaviour at scale.

papers.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
papers.summary: Cascades and scores model calls to hit a quality target at lower cost. The clearest statement of the cost-quality tradeoff that the negative cost term in this reward encodes.

papers.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
papers.summary: Generalizes chain-of-thought into an explicit search tree with lookahead and backtracking, making planning an explicit orchestration decision.

papers.title: Improving Factuality and Reasoning in Language Models through Multiagent Debate
papers.summary: Multiple model instances argue over several rounds and converge on a shared answer. Empirical evidence that adversarial critique raises factuality, which is why the Critic is a first-class agent here.

papers.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
papers.summary: Encodes standard operating procedures as agent roles with structured artifacts passed between them - the hand-designed opposite of a learned routing policy.

papers.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
papers.summary: A conversation-programming framework for composable multi-agent applications. Representative of orchestration-by-configuration rather than orchestration-by-policy.

papers.title: Dynamic LLM-Agent Network: An LLM-agent Collaboration Framework with Agent Team Optimization
papers.summary: Builds the agent interaction topology dynamically per query and optimizes team composition via importance scores - the closest published analogue of coalition selection here.

papers.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
papers.summary: Represents agent systems as computational graphs whose edges are optimized end to end, unifying prompt engineering and inter-agent orchestration as one learning problem.

papers.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
papers.summary: Learns a router between a strong and a weak model from human preference data, with an explicit cost-quality operating curve. The single-step special case of the orchestration problem posed here.
